reply_text:
I don't think this should merge yet. The function that reads the extension is wrong, so most real filenames get the wrong content type. I ran the branch's code against some edge cases on a checkout and changed nothing.

**Blocking: `extensionOf` in `src/extension.js`**

It uses `name.split('.')[1]`, which takes the text after the *first* dot. The README says it should take the text after the *last* dot, lowercased. What I got:

| Filename | Should be | Branch gives | Content type returned |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Archive.TAR.GZ` | `gz` | `TAR` | octet-stream (should be gzip) |
| `photo.JPG` | `jpg` | `JPG` | octet-stream (should be jpeg) |
| `my.photo.png` | `png` | `photo` | octet-stream (should be png) |
| `README` | `""` | `undefined` | octet-stream (only right by luck) |
| `file.` | `""` | `""` | ok |

So any uppercase extension or any name with more than one dot falls back to `application/octet-stream`. The fix is to take the text after the last dot, lowercase it, and return an empty string when there's no dot or the dot is at the end.

The tests pass only because there's one test, and it uses `photo.jpg`. It needs cases for multiple dots, uppercase, no dot and a trailing dot (the README examples work well), plus a `contentType` test.

**Worth fixing: `safeName`**

- Filenames like `..`, `...` or `.` come out as an **empty string**. Depending on how the caller builds the storage path, that could point at the upload directory itself or overwrite something. It should reject the name or use a fallback like `file`.
- Dotfiles lose their leading dot: `.htaccess` becomes `htaccess`. That's probably fine, but it's a behaviour change worth knowing about.
- The directory-climbing protection works: `a/../../b` becomes `a_.._.._b` because slashes are replaced. A null byte in `x.png\0.exe` becomes `x.png_.exe`, which is also safe.

**Minor**

- `extensionOf` will crash if it gets a missing name. Check whether the upload handler can ever pass one.
- The changelog for 0.5.0 doesn't mention the filename sanitising.
